 How to Use

 System Prompts

 Copy the contents of the relevant file into the system-prompt or custom-instructions field supported by your client or API.

 Examples include:

- API system messages

- Chatbot custom-instruction fields

- Agent-level instruction blocks

- Harness-specific system prompt configuration

 AGENTS.md Files

 Save the file as:

 AGENTS.md

 Place it in the root of the relevant repository or workspace.

 Coding agents and compatible tools can use AGENTS.md as project-level instructions.

 Workspace Policies

 Files labeled as assistant operating specification , workspace operating profile , or similar are designed for environments that support persistent global instructions.

 For example, an OpenCode installation may use:

 ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md

 The exact location depends on the client or harness being used.

 Ollama Modelfiles

 Use the supplied file directly with Ollama:

 ollama create gemma4-jb -f gemma4.md

 Adjust the output model name and source file as needed.

 Grok Configuration

 Files intended as Grok configuration should be placed in the configuration field expected by the target harness rather than inserted into the normal turn-by-turn conversation.

 Note
 Prompt behavior is highly version-dependent.

 Models are updated, instruction hierarchies change, system prompts rotate, and behavior that worked against one release may stop working against another.

 If a file appears outdated, open an issue or submit an updated version.

 Contributing

 Pull requests are welcome.

 A good contribution should follow these conventions:

-
 One prompt per file.

New files should preferably use lowercase names with hyphens and no spaces:

 model-name.md

-
 Include the complete prompt.

Contributions should be paste-ready rather than shortened summaries or excerpts.

-
 Document where it belongs.

Clearly identify whether the file is intended for a system prompt, AGENTS.md , Modelfile, configuration slot, or another instruction surface.

-
 Version changes explicitly.

Significant revisions should receive a new version rather than silently replacing an older prompt:

 opus-v3.md

-
 Keep descriptions accurate.

Avoid claiming compatibility with versions or models that have not been tested.

 Found something that no longer behaves as documented? Opening an issue with the model, version, and affected file is already useful.

 Disclaimer

 All material in this repository is provided for research and educational purposes only .

 The project exists to document prompt-level instruction behavior, instruction conflicts, persona framing, model configuration, and related LLM security concepts. This material may also help developers understand and harden systems against prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

 The maintainers do not endorse unlawful, abusive, or harmful use of this repository.

 Model providers may prohibit certain uses of these prompts under their terms of service. Users are responsible for understanding and complying with the rules, policies, and laws that apply to the systems they use.

 Star the repository if the collection saved you a session of prompt archaeology.

 Issue reports and pull requests help keep the collection current as models and instruction systems change.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 Tool
 Repo folder
 Global skills folder

 Claude Code
 .claude/
 ~/.claude/skills/

 Cursor
 .cursor/

 Codex CLI, Replit Agent
 .agents/
 ~/.agents/skills/

 Devin
 .devin/
 ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/

 GitHub Copilot
 .github/

 Gemini CLI
 .gemini/

 Google Antigravity
 .agent/
 ~/.gemini/config/skills/

 OpenCode
 .opencode/

 Grok Build
 .grok/
 ~/.grok/skills/

 Hermes Agent
 .hermes/
 ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/

 DeepSeek Harness
 .dsh/
 ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/

 Pi
 .pi/

 Qoder
 .qoder/
 ~/.qoder/skills/

 Rovo Dev
 .rovodev/
 ~/.rovodev/skills/

 Mistral Vibe
 .vibe/
 ~/.vibe/skills/

 Trae
 .trae/
 ~/.trae/skills/

 Trae China
 .trae-cn/
 ~/.trae-cn/skills/

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / * .png
 # impeccable-ignore-end

 The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> .

 Good to know

 Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/...

readmeText:
English · 简体中文

 Download Cindy  ·  Website  ·  Build with us  ·  Get help

 Cindy is an open-source AI agent, ready out of the box and yours to shape .
Connect your computers and phone, bring the models and subscriptions you already
use, and build a companion that knows how you like to work.

 All your devices. One Cindy.

 Your work computer, home desktop, laptop and phone belong together.

- Pick up the same work. Open a session from another device, continue the
conversation, and access its files without copying everything into a new chat.

- Share more than a screen. Use model providers configured on another
computer — including supported subscriptions, API providers and local models.

- Reach your whole desktop. Built-in remote desktop on your phone lets you
open apps, type and operate a connected computer when a chat isn't enough.

 Your computer becomes your server: no server rental or self-hosting setup .

 How connections and data work
 For remote access to your computers, keep them online, sign in with the same
account and enable the relevant permissions. Model sharing requires allowing
remote access to that provider; remote desktop also needs its own permissions.
Project files stay on their computer — remote access is not whole-disk sync.
Cloud companions sync their conversations, memory, skills and shared attachments
through Cindy's services; model providers process the requests sent to them.
Provider and service billing still apply.

 Keep your favorite agents. Get a better way to work.

 Already using Claude Code or Codex? Cindy brings them together with Pi ,
then adds a shared interface, multi-device access, tools and a companion of
your own.

 Harness
 What it brings

 Claude Code
 Claude Code's agent workflow, with Cindy's interface and connected tools.

 Codex
 Codex's coding workflow, available alongside your other agents.

 Pi
 A lean, open-source, extensible agent with support for multiple model providers.

 Choose a supported harness and model combination, and change it as the work
evolves. Your session stays in Cindy; switching harnesses hands off or rebuilds
the engine context rather than making their internal states identical.

 One agent not enough? Let her lead a team. Use different agents for planning,
parallel implementation and independent review, with a shared goal and clear
acceptance criteria.

 Real work, in your actual tools

 Work with your files, browser and apps. Ask for a change, inspect what happened,
and keep working from the result. Answers can include charts, interactive
controls and rich HTML , not just a wall of text.

 Build a recurring routine with automations , or hand over work through
connected chat channels such as Slack and Telegram. Connect more tools through
 Skills, plugins and MCP .

 Ready from day one. Yours to shape over time.

- Create your own companions. Give them a role, instructions, skills and
recurring work — a reviewer, researcher, project partner, or something of your own.

- Make experience reusable. Keep useful preferences and knowledge in memory;
turn a good way of working into a Skill you can reuse and share.

- Extend the product. Discover Skills and plugins in SkillHub, connect your
own tools, or build on the official plugins .

- Help shape Cindy. Audit the code, fork it, improve an interaction, fix a bug,
or contribute a useful integration. The client is Apache-2.0 licensed.

 Open source means more than visible — it means changeable.
 Build Cindy with us →

 Start with what you already have

 The client is free . Authorize a supported subscription you already pay for,
including Claude Code or Codex plans, connect your own API keys, or use a local
model. You can also use Cindy's managed model service. Provider limits and
billing still apply; the free client does not mean unlimited model usage.

 macOS · Windows · Linux · iOS · Android

 Download Cindy · Service pricing

 Linux users: see the Ubuntu, Arch Linux and Omarchy installation guide
for installation, updates, keyring setup and migration from a manual install.

 For developers

 This repository contains Cindy's open-source desktop and mobile clients and
their shared packages, organized as a pnpm monorepo.

 What's in this repo

 Path
 Description

 apps/desktop
 Electron desktop client

 apps/mobile
 Expo / React Native mobile client

 packages/*
 Shared client capabilities (auth, device-link, agent orchestration, model providers, …)

 apps/*-bin
 Tool binaries shipped with the desktop app; none are committed — claude-code, codex, and ripgrep are downloaded per platform by pnpm install , and the Android platform-tools binaries are fetched (pinned version, sha256-verified) before Windows packaging

 Not in this repo: the backend service lives in a separate
repository and is not part of this monorepo.

 Mode
 Account requirement
 Availability

 Hosted service
 Cindy cloud account
 Use Cindy's full hosted service. See pricing .

 Skip Sign-In
 No Cindy sign-in required
 Choose “Skip Sign-In” on the login screen to use local agents; the app then shows the account state as “Not signed in”. Server-backed capabilities are unavailable in this state.

 Prerequisites

- Node.js 22.x

- pnpm 10.x (v11 is not yet supported)

- Git LFS

 Getting started

 Contributor setup, Git LFS, dependency updates, and access requirements are maintained in
 CONTRIBUTING.en.md .
Plugins are installed through SkillHub or manually.

 Minimal entry point:

 git clone https://github.com/makecindy/cindy.git
 cd cindy
git lfs pull
pnpm install

 Development entry points

 # Mainland China Cindy account
pnpm restart:desktop:remote --region=cn

 # Global Cindy account
pnpm restart:desktop:remote --region=global

 Remote development uses your own Cindy cloud account and existing login state, so
you can continue existing sessions and work while developing the client. Use cn
for Mainland China accounts and global for everyone else; do not rely
on the internal default. Full desktop, mobile, data-isolation, and validation
workflows are in CONTRIBUTING.en.md .

 “Skip Sign-In” on the login screen runs local agents without a Cindy account
(shown in the app as “Not signed in”), not a connection to a local server.
Server-backed capabilities are unavailable in this state.

 About the default servers: the client connects to Cindy's official cloud
services by default (endpoint manifests in
 config/endpoint.json and
 config/endpoint.global.json ; desktop
auto-updates also come from the official CDN). This is intentional — external
developers don't need to self-host a server: sign in with your own Cindy
account in a dev build and develop / test directly against the official
servers.

 Skill Hub migration uses two separate manifest fields: released clients keep
using skillhubApiBaseUrl (the deprecated XD proxy), while current clients use
 cindySkillHubApiBaseUrl . The current client deliberately does not fall back to
the legacy field when the new endpoint is absent.

 Architecture

- DESIGN.md — visual design system, color tokens, and UI conventions

- docs/README.md — complete documentation and rules index

- docs/auth-realm-routing.md — organization SSO region discovery and session endpoint routing

- CONTRIBUTING.en.md — contributor setup, validation, and submission workflow

- AGENTS.md — engineering rules, launch/runtime contracts, and module boundaries

- docs/dev-rules/ — deep-dive architecture docs (e.g. Orca multi-agent orchestration)

 Contributing

 Contributions go through pull requests into main . Read
 CONTRIBUTING.en.md first, then use
 .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md .
Every commit needs a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off
( git commit -s ); a DCO check on each pull request enforces it, and no CLA is
required.
Please also follow CODE_OF_CONDUCT.en.md . For ordinary
usage questions, see SUPPORT.en.md ; report security issues
privately through SECURITY.en.md .

 Security

 Never commit credentials or authorization files to the working tree. If you
discover a security issue, follow SECURITY.en.md to report it
privately rather than opening a public issue.

 Privacy & telemetry

 Official distribution builds include TapDB
usage analytics for product-level aggregate statistics, including device identifiers,
OS / app version, startup and activity events. Events are associated with your account
ID after sign-in, so this is not fully anonymous. TapDB does not collect chat
content, file content, or working-directory data.

 You can disable usage analytics without editing code : on Desktop, use
Settings → About → Usage statistics; on Mobile, use Usage statistics in Settings.
The SDK checks the stored privacy-consent state and the statistics preference,
which defaults to on. Accepting the Privacy Policy records consent; a one-time
migration also records consent for eligible existing signed-in users.

 Known Mobile exception: enterprise SSO skips the policy-acceptance step. If no
analytics consent record exists and that sign-in is restored after restarting the
app, the current migration can mark even a new installation as consented. With
TapDB configured and statistics enabled, reporting can then start without explicit
policy acceptance. See Mobile sign-in restoration
and the consent migration .
Turning off Usage statistics prevents reporting from being enabled by this migration.

- Desktop stops subsequent analytics reporting immediately when disabled. Local
mode (Skip sign-in) does not report to TapDB.

- Mobile immediately unlinks the account and stops reports explicitly triggered
by Cindy. An already initialized native SDK cannot be uninitialized; fully quit
and relaunch the app to keep the SDK uninitialized.

 Implementation: Desktop consent and settings ,
 Desktop SDK ,
 Mobile consent , and
 Mobile SDK .

 Online heartbeats and diagnostic logs are separate mechanisms, unaffected by the
usage statistics switch. Desktop sends heartbeats to Cindy services only during a
verified cloud sign-in (account ID, platform, and version); local mode sends none.
Desktop native crash dumps stay local and are never uploaded automatically.
Diagnostic logs can be uploaded manually; a separate, default-off automatic crash
log upload option is also available. Log uploads require privacy consent. See the
 heartbeat implementation and
 log upload rules .

 Building from source? You are not required to keep analytics:

- Desktop development builds do not initialize TapDB by default. Explicitly setting
 XDT_TAPDB_DEV=1 lifts the build gate but still requires consent and the statistics
preference. Self-packaged Desktop builds use the same analytics gates as official
builds; you can disable analytics in Settings.

- Mobile does not initialize the SDK without injected TapDB configuration
( clientId / clientToken ). This does not mean all source builds default to off:
the self-hosted release pipeline requires nonempty configuration, while local
development permits empty values. See the
 Mobile build guide .

 License / 许可证

 Except as otherwise noted, the source code in this repository is licensed under
the Apache License, Version 2.0 . Individual source files do not
carry per-file license headers; the repository-root LICENSE governs.

 Model weights, datasets, prompts, trademarks, and other separately identified
materials may be subject to their own license terms and are not automatically
covered by the repository-level Apache-2.0 grant. Third-party open-source
components retain their own copyright and license. Their attribution notices and
SPDX SBOMs are managed under docs/legal/ , with artifact-specific
outputs in docs/legal/notices/ . See NOTICE
for this project's copyright and attribution information.

AI Design Skills

 A growing collection of design skills for AI coding tools — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and anything else that reads a markdown rules file.

 Each skill is a self-contained folder. Install the ones you need.

 Skills

 Skill
 What it does

 landing-page-design
 Builds a landing page from scratch — intake questions, page structure, conversion copy, plus a full visual system (type, spacing, radius, motion)

 More on the way. Upgrading an existing site instead of building new? That one lives in its own repo since it predates this collection.

 Install

 Pick a skill from the table above, then swap <skill-name> below for its folder name.

 Claude Code
 mkdir -p .claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills.git /tmp/ai-design-skills
cp -r /tmp/ai-design-skills/skills/ < skill-name > .claude/skills/

 Then just ask, in plain language, for what that skill covers.

 Cursor
 mkdir -p .cursor/rules
curl -o .cursor/rules/ < skill-name > .md \
 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills/main/skills/ < skill-name > /SKILL.md

 Or paste the file into Settings → Rules for AI .

 Codex / Windsurf / other
 Copy the skill's SKILL.md into whatever your tool uses for project rules:

 Tool
 Path

 Codex
 AGENTS.md

 Windsurf
 .windsurfrules

 Cline
 .clinerules

 Generic
 paste into your system prompt

 Claude.ai (no terminal)
 Download the skill's SKILL.md and upload it to a Project, or attach it to a chat and say "follow this."

 Make it yours

 Every skill's design values (fonts, colors, spacing, motion) live in one section near the bottom of its file. Fork this repo, edit that section, and the rest of the skill follows automatically.

 Credits

 landing-page-design adapts content realism and motion ideas from Leonxlnx/taste-skill by Leon Lin, MIT licensed. Details are at the end of its SKILL.md .

 License

 MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it, sell what you build with it. No attribution needed.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Jailbreaks

 A curated collection of system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, and agent operating specifications for frontier, open-weight, and free stealth models.

 About

 A working collection of 32 prompts targeting 26+ models , including complete system prompts, persona definitions, workspace policies, AGENTS.md files, configuration blocks, and Ollama Modelfiles.

 Every file is intended to be complete and paste-ready. No summaries. No partial excerpts.

 The collection covers:

- Free stealth models available through OpenCode Zen

- Open-weight families including GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Gemma, and GPT-OSS

- Closed frontier models including Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Mistral

- Coding-agent and workspace instruction formats

- Ollama Modelfiles and harness-specific configuration

 New here? Start with the collection or jump directly to how to use .

 Warning
 Research and educational purposes only.

 This repository documents how instruction hierarchies, persona framing, prompt conflicts, and policy overrides can affect model behavior. These techniques are also useful to researchers and developers studying how to make AI systems more resistant to prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

 Do not use this material to harm others, bypass applicable laws, or violate the terms of service of a platform or model provider.

 How to Use

 System Prompts

 Copy the contents of the relevant file into the system-prompt or custom-instructions field supported by your client or API.

 Examples include:

- API system messages

- Chatbot custom-instruction fields

- Agent-level instruction blocks

- Harness-specific system prompt configuration

 AGENTS.md Files

 Save the file as:

 AGENTS.md

 Place it in the root of the relevant repository or workspace.

 Coding agents and compatible tools can use AGENTS.md as project-level instructions.

 Workspace Policies

 Files labeled as assistant operating specification , workspace operating profile , or similar are designed for environments that support persistent global instructions.

 For example, an OpenCode installation may use:

 ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md

 The exact location depends on the client or harness being used.

 Ollama Modelfiles

 Use the supplied file directly with Ollama:

 ollama create gemma4-jb -f gemma4.md

 Adjust the output model name and source file as needed.

 Grok Configuration

 Files intended as Grok configuration should be placed in the configuration field expected by the target harness rather than inserted into the normal turn-by-turn conversation.

 Note
 Prompt behavior is highly version-dependent.

 Models are updated, instruction hierarchies change, system prompts rotate, and behavior that worked against one release may stop working against another.

 If a file appears outdated, open an issue or submit an updated version.

 Contributing

 Pull requests are welcome.

 A good contribution should follow these conventions:

-
 One prompt per file.

New files should preferably use lowercase names with hyphens and no spaces:

 model-name.md

-
 Include the complete prompt.

Contributions should be paste-ready rather than shortened summaries or excerpts.

-
 Document where it belongs.

Clearly identify whether the file is intended for a system prompt, AGENTS.md , Modelfile, configuration slot, or another instruction surface.

-
 Version changes explicitly.

Significant revisions should receive a new version rather than silently replacing an older prompt:

 opus-v3.md

-
 Keep descriptions accurate.

Avoid claiming compatibility with versions or models that have not been tested.

 Found something that no longer behaves as documented? Opening an issue with the model, version, and affected file is already useful.

 Disclaimer

 All material in this repository is provided for research and educational purposes only .

 The project exists to document prompt-level instruction behavior, instruction conflicts, persona framing, model configuration, and related LLM security concepts. This material may also help developers understand and harden systems against prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

 The maintainers do not endorse unlawful, abusive, or harmful use of this repository.

 Model providers may prohibit certain uses of these prompts under their terms of service. Users are responsible for understanding and complying with the rules, policies, and laws that apply to the systems they use.

 Star the repository if the collection saved you a session of prompt archaeology.

 Issue reports and pull requests help keep the collection current as models and instruction systems change.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / * .png
 # impeccable-ignore-end

 The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> .

 Good to know

 Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/...

readmeText:
OpenBot

 OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. It supports the local
 Codex App Server and
 Claude Code , plus Grok CLI ,
OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor CLI , and Cline CLI through ACP. It gives every agent its own workspace and
conversation, and provides local queues, file transfers, an embedded browser, and agent-to-agent
messaging in one desktop app.

 Warning
 OpenBot is a development preview. Agents currently run with danger-full-access and
 approvalPolicy: never . They can read and modify files, run commands, use the network, and control
the embedded browser without per-action confirmations after the explicit first-launch consent.
Run only agents and tasks you trust, keep backups, and review Security before use.

 What works

- Prompt-driven agent creation and editing on desktop and mobile, with editable instructions, avatar, and section review before saving.

- Persistent agents backed by independent Codex, Claude, Grok, OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor, or Cline sessions and local workspaces.

- Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints and custom ACP agents, with detection of local model servers (Ollama, LM Studio) and installed agents.

- Per-agent context monitoring with automatic compaction before long threads exhaust the model window.

- FIFO message queues with pause, resume, cancellation, and crash-safe persistence.

- Agent-to-agent messages, replies, reactions, images, and managed file transfers.

- Shared desktop channel chats with one task owner, explicit delegation, shared history, and Stop, Resume, Reassign, Archive, and Restore controls.

- A persistent embedded browser that agents can open, inspect, and control.

- Optional Computer Use on macOS, Windows and Linux through the cua-driver binary in the release, which OpenBot starts as its own child process and gives to every provider.

- Per-agent model, reasoning, profile, notification, browser, and panel state.

- Local data and privacy-safe diagnostics exports from the account menu.

- Optional OpenBot accounts through one-time email codes. The account API runs on Cloudflare Workers and D1.

 OpenBot is local-first, not offline-only. Codex connects to OpenAI, Claude connects to Anthropic,
Grok connects to xAI, Gemini connects to Google, Cursor connects to Cursor, Cline connects to Cline,
visited pages use the network, and installed plugins may connect to their own services.

 Install

 OpenBot supports macOS 13 or newer on Apple silicon or Intel, Windows 10 or newer on x64 systems, and x64
or arm64 Linux as an AppImage.

 macOS

- Download the latest OpenBot-*-arm64.dmg (or OpenBot-*-x64.dmg on an Intel Mac) from GitHub Releases .

- Drag OpenBot to Applications and open it.

 Windows

- Download the latest OpenBot-*-x64.exe from GitHub Releases .

- Run the installer and open OpenBot.

 Linux

- Download the latest OpenBot-*-x86_64.AppImage (or OpenBot-*-arm64.AppImage on arm64) from GitHub Releases .

- Make it executable with chmod +x OpenBot-*.AppImage , then run it.

 The AppImage does not need libfuse2, so it also runs on Arch Linux and Omarchy. It mounts itself
with fusermount3 from the fuse3 package.

 On Ubuntu 23.10 or newer and on Debian 13, unprivileged user namespaces are restricted by AppArmor
and OpenBot exits during launch until you install an AppArmor profile:

 sudo install -m 0644 build/linux/openbot.apparmor /etc/apparmor.d/openbot
sudo systemctl reload apparmor

 The same file ships inside the AppImage at resources/linux/openbot.apparmor . Edit the attachment
path in the profile if you keep the AppImage outside the usual locations. Do not start OpenBot with
 --no-sandbox : that removes the boundary between a renderer and the rest of the computer.

 On the first start from an AppImage, OpenBot writes ~/.local/share/applications/openbot.desktop
and ~/.local/share/icons/openbot.png , which is what lets an openbot:// link - an invitation, or
a plugin listing - open the app and gives the launcher an icon that stays after the app exits. Delete the two files to undo it.

 Remote desktop works on Linux x64 in an X11 session,
such as Xorg or Xvfb. It does not work under Wayland, and the arm64 AppImage does not include it.

 For Gemini sign-in, install a desktop browser and xdg-utils . Open the sign-in page in a
desktop session on the same host or VM. Google sends the callback to that host through
 127.0.0.1 ; a server with no desktop cannot complete this sign-in. See
 Gemini setup .

 Linux server with no screen

 To run OpenBot as an always-on server of your account on a VPS or home server (Ubuntu 24.04 or
26.04 with systemd), install it from a terminal and sign in with an email code:

 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nightly-labs/openbot/main/scripts/install-server.sh | sudo bash
sudo openbot login

 Then use it from the desktop app, the iPhone app or openbot.run/app . See
 self-hosted servers for the options and the openbot commands.

 Docker

 The same server runs as a container ( linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 ). The seccomp profile lets the
Electron sandbox stay on:

 curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nightly-labs/openbot/main/docker/seccomp.json
docker run -d --name openbot --restart unless-stopped \
 --security-opt seccomp=seccomp.json --security-opt no-new-privileges:true \
 --shm-size 1g --stop-timeout 60 -v openbot-data:/data \
 ghcr.io/nightly-labs/openbot:latest
docker exec -it openbot openbot login

 See Docker for Compose, the data volume, upgrades and the security limits. For Amazon ECS,
see AWS ECS .

 Nix

 The flake installs the desktop app from the latest release on x64 or arm64 Linux and on Apple silicon:

 nix run github:nightly-labs/openbot
nix profile install github:nightly-labs/openbot

 overlays.default adds pkgs.openbot . OpenBot is not free software, so your nixpkgs must allow it,
for example with nixpkgs.config.allowUnfreePredicate = pkg: lib.getName pkg == "openbot"; .
Nix installs OpenBot updates. OpenBot does not update itself from the Nix store. On Linux, the Nix
package does not include the remote desktop runtime, because nixpkgs does not have a library that it
needs.

 Important
 Windows releases are signed by SYNTHETIFY LABS SPÓŁKA Z OGRANICZONĄ ODPOWIEDZIALNOŚCIĄ . Older
releases are not code-signed. SmartScreen can still warn about a new release. Check the release
checksum or GitHub build attestation before you run the installer.

 Agent setup

 OpenBot can download a supported provider runtime when you select Download in onboarding,
Settings, agent setup, or the model picker. OpenBot prefers its managed CLI. Explicit OPENBOT_*_PATH overrides take precedence; a compatible
system CLI is used when no managed copy is available. OpenBot checks for a newer provider CLI
release at startup and every hour, and Check for updates in a provider's actions menu checks at
once. Updates install the latest upstream release without changing the user’s system CLI; the
version in native-runtime.lock.json is only the first-install fallback.

 You can also install a CLI yourself.

 Codex CLI on macOS:

 curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh

 Claude CLI on macOS:

 curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

 Install Grok CLI following the Grok Build documentation , then
authenticate with grok login or set XAI_API_KEY in the environment used to launch OpenBot.

 OpenBot downloads and pins the OpenCode CLI, like Codex, Claude, and Grok. OpenCode's free models
need no account and no sign-in: select OpenCode, click Connect, and OpenBot reads the models that
the CLI advertises. To use the paid OpenCode Go models, click Sign in on the OpenCode row and
paste a Go key from opencode.ai/auth . OpenBot encrypts the key on this
computer and gives it only to the local CLI. OpenBot supports OpenCode Go only: the Zen models a
Go key does not buy stay out of the picker. Models with the Free label in the model picker need no
sign-in. Other models need a sign-in with their provider: a Go key for the opencode-go/ models, or
 opencode auth login in a terminal for OpenCode Zen and third-party providers. Without it, the turn
fails with an error that names the provider. If you installed OpenCode yourself, OpenBot
keeps that install and offers no download. Set OPENBOT_OPENCODE_PATH to select an executable
outside your shell's search path. Remote OpenCode agents require Team API v4; older clients do not
show these agents.

 Gemini uses a Google AI Pro or Ultra plan. OpenBot downloads Google's Antigravity ACP server on
this computer when you select Download on the Gemini row, because Google's license does not let
OpenBot include it. Sign in opens Google's sign-in page in your browser. OpenBot never uses an
 antigravity command on your search path, because the Antigravity editor installs a command with
that name. Set OPENBOT_ANTIGRAVITY_PATH to select a server executable yourself. Put it in a
 bin/ folder, and put an antigravity-package.json file with its version in the folder above
 bin/ . Keep localharness_external beside the server. When that path is set, OpenBot uses
only it. Connect remains available in the host's local Settings > Providers screen. Remote
settings cannot perform Google sign-in; use a browser on the host. See
 Gemini setup and download recovery for the required
layout, the reported IPv6 download failure, and checks that do not change host networking.

 Cursor uses a Cursor plan or a Cursor API key. OpenBot downloads and pins the Cursor CLI
( cursor-agent ) when you select Download on the Cursor row in More providers, and starts it with
 cursor-agent acp . Sign in opens Cursor's sign-in page in your browser. You can also set
 CURSOR_API_KEY in the environment used to launch OpenBot. If you installed cursor-agent
yourself, OpenBot uses it until a download exists. OpenBot never uses the cursor command, which
starts the Cursor editor. Set OPENBOT_CURSOR_PATH to select an executable yourself. Cursor
agents stay on this computer: team members do not see them.

 Cline uses a Cline account, which has free models with limits for each model. The provider of a
free model can use your prompts to train models. OpenBot downloads and pins the Cline CLI ( cline ) when you
select Download on the Cline row in More providers, and starts it with cline --acp . Sign in opens
Cline's sign-in page in your browser. You can also set CLINE_API_KEY in the environment used to
launch OpenBot. If you installed cline 3.0.68 or newer yourself, OpenBot uses it until a download
exists. Set OPENBOT_CLINE_PATH to select an executable yourself. Cline agents stay on this
computer: team members do not see them.

 On Windows, install the native CLI and make sure codex , claude , or grok is available in PowerShell.
Claude Code also requires Git for Windows. Then authenticate the installed CLI and restart OpenBot.

 Bun and Node.js are not required when using an installed release. Optional Computer Use works on
macOS, Windows and Linux, and the release carries the driver, so there is nothing to install. Only
macOS asks for a permission for it: Screen Recording and Accessibility.

 OpenBot uses the existing local CLI login. It does not copy provider credentials. Grok's
 XAI_API_KEY and per-session MCP bearer tokens are never persisted or logged. Each provider's terms
apply to your sign-in. See provider terms for Claude subscriptions.

 For setup problems, data reset, and uninstall instructions, see
 Troubleshooting . OpenBot's data and network behavior is documented in
 Privacy .

 Development

 Development requires stable Bun 1.4.2, Node.js 24 (the version in .nvmrc , matching
the Node that Electron bundles - run nvm use ), and at least one supported agent CLI.

 Install the exact Bun version on macOS or Linux:

 curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash -s " bun-v1.4.2 "

 Install it on Windows in PowerShell:

 iex " & { $ ( irm https: // bun.com / install.ps1 ) } -Version 1.4.2 "

 git clone https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot.git
 cd openbot
bun insta...

representativeRepos.readmeText:
AI Design Skills

 A growing collection of design skills for AI coding tools — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and anything else that reads a markdown rules file.

 Each skill is a self-contained folder. Install the ones you need.

 Skills

 Skill
 What it does

 landing-page-design
 Builds a landing page from scratch — intake questions, page structure, conversion copy, plus a full visual system (type, spacing, radius, motion)

 More on the way. Upgrading an existing site instead of building new? That one lives in its own repo since it predates this collection.

 Install

 Pick a skill from the table above, then swap <skill-name> below for its folder name.

 Claude Code
 mkdir -p .claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills.git /tmp/ai-design-skills
cp -r /tmp/ai-design-skills/skills/ < skill-name > .claude/skills/

 Then just ask, in plain language, for what that skill covers.

 Cursor
 mkdir -p .cursor/rules
curl -o .cursor/rules/ < skill-name > .md \
 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills/main/skills/ < skill-name > /SKILL.md

 Or paste the file into Settings → Rules for AI .

 Codex / Windsurf / other
 Copy the skill's SKILL.md into whatever your tool uses for project rules:

 Tool
 Path

 Codex
 AGENTS.md

 Windsurf
 .windsurfrules

 Cline
 .clinerules

 Generic
 paste into your system prompt

 Claude.ai (no terminal)
 Download the skill's SKILL.md and upload it to a Project, or attach it to a chat and say "follow this."

 Make it yours

 Every skill's design values (fonts, colors, spacing, motion) live in one section near the bottom of its file. Fork this repo, edit that section, and the rest of the skill follows automatically.

 Credits

 landing-page-design adapts content realism and motion ideas from Leonxlnx/taste-skill by Leon Lin, MIT licensed. Details are at the end of its SKILL.md .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Jailbreaks

 A curated collection of system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, and agent operating specifications for frontier, open-weight, and free stealth models.

 About

 A working collection of 32 prompts targeting 26+ models , including complete system prompts, persona definitions, workspace policies, AGENTS.md files, configuration blocks, and Ollama Modelfiles.

 Every file is intended to be complete and paste-ready. No summaries. No partial excerpts.

 The collection covers:

- Free stealth models available through OpenCode Zen

- Open-weight families including GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Gemma, and GPT-OSS

- Closed frontier models including Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Mistral

- Coding-agent and workspace instruction formats

- Ollama Modelfiles and harness-specific configuration

 New here? Start with the collection or jump directly to how to use .

 Warning
 Research and educational purposes only.

 This repository documents how instruction hierarchies, persona framing, prompt conflicts, and policy overrides can affect model behavior. These techniques are also useful to researchers and developers studying how to make AI systems more resistant to prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

 Do not use this material to harm others, bypass applicable laws, or violate the terms of service of a platform or model provider.

 How to Use

 System Prompts

 Copy the contents of the relevant file into the system-prompt or custom-instructions field supported by your client or API.

 Examples include:

- API system messages

- Chatbot custom-instruction fields

- Agent-level instruction blocks

- Harness-specific system prompt configuration

 AGENTS.md Files

 Save the file as:

 AGENTS.md

 Place it in the root of the relevant repository or workspace.

 Coding agents and compatible tools can use AGENTS.md as project-level instructions.

 Workspace Policies

 Files labeled as assistant operating specification , workspace operating profile , or similar are designed for environments that support persistent global instructions.

 For example, an OpenCode installation may use:

 ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md

 The exact location depends on the client or harness being used.

 Ollama Modelfiles

 Use the supplied file directly with Ollama:

 ollama create gemma4-jb -f gemma4.md

 Adjust the output model name and source file as needed.

 Grok Configuration

 Files intended as Grok configuration should be placed in the configuration field expected by the target harness rather than inserted into the normal turn-by-turn conversation.

 Note
 Prompt behavior is highly version-dependent.

 Models are updated, instruction hierarchies change, system prompts rotate, and behavior that worked against one release may stop working against another.

 If a file appears outdated, open an issue or submit an updated version.

 Contributing

 Pull requests are welcome.

 A good contribution should follow these conventions:

-
 One prompt per file.

New files should preferably use lowercase names with hyphens and no spaces:

 model-name.md

-
 Include the complete prompt.

Contributions should be paste-ready rather than shortened summaries or excerpts.

-
 Document where it belongs.

Clearly identify whether the file is intended for a system prompt, AGENTS.md , Modelfile, configuration slot, or another instruction surface.

-
 Version changes explicitly.

Significant revisions should receive a new version rather than silently replacing an older prompt:

 opus-v3.md

-
 Keep descriptions accurate.

Avoid claiming compatibility with versions or models that have not been tested.

 Found something that no longer behaves as documented? Opening an issue with the model, version, and affected file is already useful.

 Disclaimer

 All material in this repository is provided for research and educational purposes only .

 The project exists to document prompt-level instruction behavior, instruction conflicts, persona framing, model configuration, and related LLM security concepts. This material may also help developers understand and harden systems against prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

 The maintainers do not endorse unlawful, abusive, or harmful use of this repository.

 Model providers may prohibit certain uses of these prompts under their terms of service. Users are responsible for understanding and complying with the rules, policies, and laws that apply to the systems they use.

 Star the repository if the collection saved you a session of prompt archaeology.

 Issue reports and pull requests help keep the collection current as models and instruction systems change.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 Tool
 Repo folder
 Global skills folder

 Claude Code
 .claude/
 ~/.claude/skills/

 Cursor
 .cursor/

 Codex CLI, Replit Agent
 .agents/
 ~/.agents/skills/

 Devin
 .devin/
 ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/

 GitHub Copilot
 .github/

 Gemini CLI
 .gemini/

 Google Antigravity
 .agent/
 ~/.gemini/config/skills/

 OpenCode
 .opencode/

 Grok Build
 .grok/
 ~/.grok/skills/

 Hermes Agent
 .hermes/
 ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/

 DeepSeek Harness
 .dsh/
 ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/

 Pi
 .pi/

 Qoder
 .qoder/
 ~/.qoder/skills/

 Rovo Dev
 .rovodev/
 ~/.rovodev/skills/

 Mistral Vibe
 .vibe/
 ~/.vibe/skills/

 Trae
 .trae/
 ~/.trae/skills/

 Trae China
 .trae-cn/
 ~/.trae-cn/skills/

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / * .png
 # impeccable-ignore-end

 The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> .

 Good to know

 Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/...

readmeText:
Jailbreaks

 A curated collection of system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, and agent operating specifications for frontier, open-weight, and free stealth models.

 About

 A working collection of 32 prompts targeting 26+ models , including complete system prompts, persona definitions, workspace policies, AGENTS.md files, configuration blocks, and Ollama Modelfiles.

 Every file is intended to be complete and paste-ready. No summaries. No partial excerpts.

 The collection covers:

- Free stealth models available through OpenCode Zen

- Open-weight families including GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Gemma, and GPT-OSS

- Closed frontier models including Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Mistral

- Coding-agent and workspace instruction formats

- Ollama Modelfiles and harness-specific configuration

 New here? Start with the collection or jump directly to how to use .

 Warning
 Research and educational purposes only.

 This repository documents how instruction hierarchies, persona framing, prompt conflicts, and policy overrides can affect model behavior. These techniques are also useful to researchers and developers studying how to make AI systems more resistant to prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

 Do not use this material to harm others, bypass applicable laws, or violate the terms of service of a platform or model provider.
