representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 Tool
 Repo folder
 Global skills folder

 Claude Code
 .claude/
 ~/.claude/skills/

 Cursor
 .cursor/

 Codex CLI, Replit Agent
 .agents/
 ~/.agents/skills/

 Devin
 .devin/
 ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/

 GitHub Copilot
 .github/

 Gemini CLI
 .gemini/

 Google Antigravity
 .agent/
 ~/.gemini/config/skills/

 OpenCode
 .opencode/

 Grok Build
 .grok/
 ~/.grok/skills/

 Hermes Agent
 .hermes/
 ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/

 DeepSeek Harness
 .dsh/
 ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/

 Pi
 .pi/

 Qoder
 .qoder/
 ~/.qoder/skills/

 Rovo Dev
 .rovodev/
 ~/.rovodev/skills/

 Mistral Vibe
 .vibe/
 ~/.vibe/skills/

 Trae
 .trae/
 ~/.trae/skills/

 Trae China
 .trae-cn/
 ~/.trae-cn/skills/

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / * .png
 # impeccable-ignore-end

 The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> .

 Good to know

 Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/...

readmeText:
the-craft-of-selfteaching

 One has no future if one couldn't teach themself [1] .

 自学是门手艺

 没有自学能力的人没有未来

 作者：李笑来

 特别感谢 霍炬 （ @virushuo ）、 洪强宁 （ @hongqn ) 两位良师诤友在此书写作过程中给予我的巨大帮助！

 # pseudo-code of selfteaching in Python

 def teach_yourself ( anything ):
 while not create ():
 learn ()
 practice ()
 return teach_yourself ( another )

 teach_yourself ( coding )

 请先行阅读 T-appendix.jupyter-installation-and-setup 以便在本地安装 Jupyterlab 而后就能用更好的体验阅读本书。

 有兴趣帮忙的朋友，请先行阅读 如何使用 Pull Request 为这本书校对 。

 2019 年 3 月 23 日，新增 Markdown 版本：

 https://github.com/selfteaching/the-craft-of-selfteaching/tree/master/markdown

 目录

- 01.preface（ 前言 ）

- 02.proof-of-work（ 如何证明你真的读过这本书？ ）

- Part.1.A.better.teachyourself（ 为什么一定要掌握自学能力？ ）

- Part.1.B.why.start.from.learning.coding（ 为什么把编程当作自学的入口？ ）

- Part.1.C.must.learn.sth.only.by.reading（ 只靠阅读习得新技能 ）

- Part.1.D.preparation.for.reading（ 开始阅读前的一些准备 ）

- Part.1.E.1.entrance（ 入口 ）

- Part.1.E.2.values-and-their-operators（ 值及其相应的运算 ）

- Part.1.E.3.controlflow（ 流程控制 ）

- Part.1.E.4.functions（ 函数 ）

- Part.1.E.5.strings（ 字符串 ）

- Part.1.E.6.containers（ 数据容器 ）

AI Design Skills

 A growing collection of design skills for AI coding tools — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and anything else that reads a markdown rules file.

 Each skill is a self-contained folder. Install the ones you need.

 Skills

 Skill
 What it does

 landing-page-design
 Builds a landing page from scratch — intake questions, page structure, conversion copy, plus a full visual system (type, spacing, radius, motion)

 More on the way. Upgrading an existing site instead of building new? That one lives in its own repo since it predates this collection.

 Install

 Pick a skill from the table above, then swap <skill-name> below for its folder name.

 Claude Code
 mkdir -p .claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills.git /tmp/ai-design-skills
cp -r /tmp/ai-design-skills/skills/ < skill-name > .claude/skills/

 Then just ask, in plain language, for what that skill covers.

 Cursor
 mkdir -p .cursor/rules
curl -o .cursor/rules/ < skill-name > .md \
 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills/main/skills/ < skill-name > /SKILL.md

 Or paste the file into Settings → Rules for AI .

 Codex / Windsurf / other
 Copy the skill's SKILL.md into whatever your tool uses for project rules:

 Tool
 Path

 Codex
 AGENTS.md

 Windsurf
 .windsurfrules

 Cline
 .clinerules

 Generic
 paste into your system prompt

 Claude.ai (no terminal)
 Download the skill's SKILL.md and upload it to a Project, or attach it to a chat and say "follow this."

 Make it yours

 Every skill's design values (fonts, colors, spacing, motion) live in one section near the bottom of its file. Fork this repo, edit that section, and the rest of the skill follows automatically.

 Credits

 landing-page-design adapts content realism and motion ideas from Leonxlnx/taste-skill by Leon Lin, MIT licensed. Details are at the end of its SKILL.md .

 License

 MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it, sell what you build with it. No attribution needed.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Jailbreaks

 A curated collection of system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, and agent operating specifications for frontier, open-weight, and free stealth models.

 About

 A working collection of 32 prompts targeting 26+ models , including complete system prompts, persona definitions, workspace policies, AGENTS.md files, configuration blocks, and Ollama Modelfiles.

 Every file is intended to be complete and paste-ready. No summaries. No partial excerpts.

 The collection covers:

- Free stealth models available through OpenCode Zen

- Open-weight families including GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Gemma, and GPT-OSS

- Closed frontier models including Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Mistral

- Coding-agent and workspace instruction formats

- Ollama Modelfiles and harness-specific configuration

 New here? Start with the collection or jump directly to how to use .

 Warning
 Research and educational purposes only.

 This repository documents how instruction hierarchies, persona framing, prompt conflicts, and policy overrides can affect model behavior. These techniques are also useful to researchers and developers studying how to make AI systems more resistant to prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

 Do not use this material to harm others, bypass applicable laws, or violate the terms of service of a platform or model provider.

 How to Use

 System Prompts

 Copy the contents of the relevant file into the system-prompt or custom-instructions field supported by your client or API.

 Examples include:

- API system messages

- Chatbot custom-instruction fields

- Agent-level instruction blocks

- Harness-specific system prompt configuration

 AGENTS.md Files

 Save the file as:

 AGENTS.md

 Place it in the root of the relevant repository or workspace.

 Coding agents and compatible tools can use AGENTS.md as project-level instructions.

 Workspace Policies

 Files labeled as assistant operating specification , workspace operating profile , or similar are designed for environments that support persistent global instructions.

 For example, an OpenCode installation may use:

 ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md

 The exact location depends on the client or harness being used.

 Ollama Modelfiles

 Use the supplied file directly with Ollama:

 ollama create gemma4-jb -f gemma4.md

 Adjust the output model name and source file as needed.

 Grok Configuration

 Files intended as Grok configuration should be placed in the configuration field expected by the target harness rather than inserted into the normal turn-by-turn conversation.

 Note
 Prompt behavior is highly version-dependent.

 Models are updated, instruction hierarchies change, system prompts rotate, and behavior that worked against one release may stop working against another.

 If a file appears outdated, open an issue or submit an updated version.

 Contributing

 Pull requests are welcome.

 A good contribution should follow these conventions:

-
 One prompt per file.

New files should preferably use lowercase names with hyphens and no spaces:

 model-name.md

-
 Include the complete prompt.

Contributions should be paste-ready rather than shortened summaries or excerpts.

-
 Document where it belongs.

Clearly identify whether the file is intended for a system prompt, AGENTS.md , Modelfile, configuration slot, or another instruction surface.

-
 Version changes explicitly.

Significant revisions should receive a new version rather than silently replacing an older prompt:

 opus-v3.md

-
 Keep descriptions accurate.

Avoid claiming compatibility with versions or models that have not been tested.

 Found something that no longer behaves as documented? Opening an issue with the model, version, and affected file is already useful.

 Disclaimer

 All material in this repository is provided for research and educational purposes only .

 The project exists to document prompt-level instruction behavior, instruction conflicts, persona framing, model configuration, and related LLM security concepts. This material may also help developers understand and harden systems against prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

 The maintainers do not endorse unlawful, abusive, or harmful use of this repository.

 Model providers may prohibit certain uses of these prompts under their terms of service. Users are responsible for understanding and complying with the rules, policies, and laws that apply to the systems they use.

 Star the repository if the collection saved you a session of prompt archaeology.

 Issue reports and pull requests help keep the collection current as models and instruction systems change.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / * .png
 # impeccable-ignore-end

 The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> .

 Good to know

 Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/...

readmeText:
security-audit

 A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

 This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness . The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

 What it does

 The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

- Reconnaissance -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in architecture.md and coverage-ledger.json .

- Coverage-led hunting -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.

- Candidate validation -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.

- Structured output -- write confirmed , needs_validation , and rejected records to findings.json and validate them against report-schema.json .

- Independent record verification -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.

- Target-neutral reporting -- derive REPORT.md , FINDINGS-DETAIL.md , and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md from the verified records and coverage ledger.

 The parent runs validate-coverage-ledger.cjs after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs validate-findings.cjs in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

 The verdicts are distinct: confirmed has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, needs_validation has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and rejected records a disproved candidate.

 Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

 Files

 File
 Purpose

 SKILL.md
 Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns

 RECONNAISSANCE.md
 Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions

 HUNTING.md
 Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules

 ATTACK-CLASSES.md
 Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts

 MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md
 Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets

 AI-AND-LLM.md
 Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets

 WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md
 HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets

 CLIENT-SIDE.md
 DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets

 SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md
 Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes

 CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md
 IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes

 PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md
 RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes

 RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md
 Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes

 DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md
 Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes

 DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md
 Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes

 VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md
 Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting

 report-schema.json
 JSON schema for all three findings.json verdicts

 validate-findings.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for findings.json in Phases 4 and 5

 validate-findings.test.cjs
 Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks

 validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for coverage-ledger.json in Phases 1–5

 validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs
 Coverage-ledger validator tests

 Installation

 Install the skill with the Skills CLI :

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit

 Use --global for a user-level installation:

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit \
 --global

 Run npx skills --help for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

 Usage

 Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

 security audit this codebase

 find security vulnerabilities in ./src

 do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project

 The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N> . The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

 Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents

- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators

- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as needs_validation instead of executing target code.

 Design principles

- Only confirm established boundary failures. Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as needs_validation with its exact unresolved fact.

- Adversarial validation. The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.

- Severity requires impact. Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.

- Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities. If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.

- Multiple runs improve coverage. In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

 Contact

 Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

 License

 MIT -- see LICENSE .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
security-audit

 A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

 This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness . The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

 What it does

 The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

- Reconnaissance -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in architecture.md and coverage-ledger.json .

- Coverage-led hunting -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.

- Candidate validation -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.

- Structured output -- write confirmed , needs_validation , and rejected records to findings.json and validate them against report-schema.json .

- Independent record verification -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.

- Target-neutral reporting -- derive REPORT.md , FINDINGS-DETAIL.md , and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md from the verified records and coverage ledger.

 The parent runs validate-coverage-ledger.cjs after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs validate-findings.cjs in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

 The verdicts are distinct: confirmed has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, needs_validation has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and rejected records a disproved candidate.

 Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

 Files

 File
 Purpose

 SKILL.md
 Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns

 RECONNAISSANCE.md
 Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions

 HUNTING.md
 Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules

 ATTACK-CLASSES.md
 Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts

 MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md
 Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets

 AI-AND-LLM.md
 Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets

 WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md
 HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets

 CLIENT-SIDE.md
 DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets

 SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md
 Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes

 CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md
 IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes

 PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md
 RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes

 RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md
 Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes

 DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md
 Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes

 DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md
 Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes

 VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md
 Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting

 report-schema.json
 JSON schema for all three findings.json verdicts

 validate-findings.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for findings.json in Phases 4 and 5

 validate-findings.test.cjs
 Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks

 validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for coverage-ledger.json in Phases 1–5

 validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs
 Coverage-ledger validator tests

 Installation

 Install the skill with the Skills CLI :

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit

 Use --global for a user-level installation:

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit \
 --global

 Run npx skills --help for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

 Usage

 Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

 security audit this codebase

 find security vulnerabilities in ./src

 do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project

 The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N> . The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

 Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents

- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators

- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as needs_validation instead of executing target code.

 Design principles

- Only confirm established boundary failures. Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as needs_validation with its exact unresolved fact.

- Adversarial validation. The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.

- Severity requires impact. Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.

- Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities. If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.

- Multiple runs improve coverage. In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

 Contact

 Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

 License

 MIT -- see LICENSE .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 Tool
 Repo folder
 Global skills folder

 Claude Code
 .claude/
 ~/.claude/skills/

 Cursor
 .cursor/

 Codex CLI, Replit Agent
 .agents/
 ~/.agents/skills/

 Devin
 .devin/
 ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/

 GitHub Copilot
 .github/

 Gemini CLI
 .gemini/

 Google Antigravity
 .agent/
 ~/.gemini/config/skills/

 OpenCode
 .opencode/

 Grok Build
 .grok/
 ~/.grok/skills/

 Hermes Agent
 .hermes/
 ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/

 DeepSeek Harness
 .dsh/
 ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/

 Pi
 .pi/

 Qoder
 .qoder/
 ~/.qoder/skills/

 Rovo Dev
 .rovodev/
 ~/.rovodev/skills/

 Mistral Vibe
 .vibe/
 ~/.vibe/skills/

 Trae
 .trae/
 ~/.trae/skills/

 Trae China
 .trae-cn/
 ~/.trae-cn/skills/

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / * .png
 # impeccable-ignore-end

 The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> .

 Good to know

 Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/...

 Cut agent token spend by 80%. Graphify Cloud is always-on memory that governs your agents, keeps code quality high, and proves correctness with formal verification. Start a free 14-day trial →

 Type /graphify in your AI coding assistant and it maps your entire project (code, docs, PDFs, images, videos) into a knowledge graph you can query instead of grepping through files.

- Code maps for free, fully local. Code is parsed with tree-sitter AST: deterministic, no LLM, nothing leaves your machine. (Docs, PDFs, images and video use your assistant's model, or a configured API key, for a semantic pass.)

- Every edge is explained. Each connection is tagged EXTRACTED (explicit in the source) or INFERRED (resolved by graphify), so you can tell what was read directly from what was inferred.

- Not a vector index. No embeddings, no vector store: a real graph you traverse. Ask a question, trace the path between two things, or explain one concept.

Factory Droid uses the Task tool for parallel subagent dispatch. OpenClaw and Aider use sequential extraction (parallel agent support is still early on those platforms). Trae uses the Agent tool for parallel subagent dispatch and does not support PreToolUse hooks, so AGENTS.md is the always-on mechanism.

 --platform agents (alias --platform skills ) targets the generic cross-framework Agent-Skills locations: the spec's user-global ~/.agents/skills/ (read by npx skills and spec-compliant frameworks) for a global install, and ./.agents/skills/ for a project ( --project ) install. The bare graphify install stays single-platform (Claude Code) by design: use the named agents platform when you want the skill discoverable by any framework that reads .agents/skills .

 Pi has no PreToolUse hook, so graphify pi guard install registers a native Pi extension (via Pi's own pi install <package directory> ) that runs the installed graphify hook-guard before Pi's read , grep , find and search-style bash calls. Fresh/stale graph decisions and the GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT=1 once-per-session indexed-read denial come from that same policy, so Pi matches Claude Code's hook behavior; guidance arrives as a <system-reminder source="graphify"> steering message. It needs Pi 0.58.4 or newer: earlier versions let a steering message skip the rest of a parallel tool-call batch. The package ships inside the Graphify installation, so install Graphify persistently ( uv tool install graphifyy or pipx install graphifyy , not uvx ), restart Pi after installing or upgrading, and remove it with graphify pi guard uninstall . Only local file targets are inspected; the hook needs graphify on an absolute PATH entry outside the project, is bounded to a two-second, 256 KiB-in/64 KiB-out call, and fails open. The same package also loads in Oh My Pi : omp plugin install "$(graphify pi guard path)" . The registered path contains the Python version and venv, so re-run graphify pi guard install after changing either, and remove the old entry with pi remove <old path> .

 Claude SEO is a free SEO plugin for Claude Code. Give it any website and it runs a full SEO audit in 10 to 15 minutes, then hands you a clear action plan, sorted by what matters most.

 It checks everything a good SEO consultant would:

- Technical SEO. Crawlability, indexing, sitemaps, robots.txt, redirects, page speed and Core Web Vitals.

- Content quality. E-E-A-T (experience, expertise, authority and trust), thin pages and topic coverage.

- Structured data. Finds, validates and writes Schema.org markup for rich results.

- AI search (GEO). How likely Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini are to cite your pages.

- Local and e-commerce SEO. Google Business Profile, reviews, map pack, product pages and international sites.

 Claude SEO is built from 26 sub-skills and 19 specialist agents, and up to 17 agents work on your site at the same time. Every recommendation explains why it matters and how you will know it worked.

 See it in action

 Type /seo in Claude Code to see every command:

 Run a full audit and watch the agents fan out across the site:

 Watch the full demo on YouTube

 Real results

 The project's own site, claude-seo.md , audited with Claude SEO from day one: 10.8K Search Console clicks in its first 12 weeks and a 99 mobile PageSpeed score.

 How an audit works

- It learns your site. Claude SEO detects the type of business (SaaS, local, e-commerce, publisher or agency) and adjusts its checks.

- The team fans out. Up to 17 specialist agents audit the site in parallel: technical, content, schema, speed, AI search and more.

- You get a plan, not a pile of warnings. Findings are scored and sorted into a prioritized action plan. Each recommendation says what it is based on, what it depends on and how you will know it worked.

 Reports are saved as Markdown, and /seo google report turns them into a polished PDF.

 ** Critical Issue: ** The ` founder ` property only includes Daniel Agrici.
Benjamin Samar (Co-Founder and Technical Director) is displayed on the page
but absent from the schema. This content-schema mismatch can confuse search engines.

 Want the details? Read the methodology and the architecture .

 Install

 You need Claude Code 1.0.33 or newer. Run these three commands inside it:

 /plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-seo
/plugin install claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo
/seo setup

 /seo setup prepares everything Claude SEO needs (its own Python environment and a headless browser) without touching the rest of your system. Run /seo doctor any time to check it.

 Manual install: macOS and Linux

 git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.git
bash claude-seo/install.sh

 One-liner (curl, review then run):

 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo/main/install.sh > install.sh
cat install.sh # review before running
bash install.sh
rm install.sh

 Manual install: Windows (PowerShell)

 git clone -- depth 1 https: // github.com / AgriciDaniel / claude - seo.git
powershell - ExecutionPolicy Bypass - File claude - seo\install.ps1

 Why git clone instead of irm | iex ? Claude Code's own security guardrails flag irm ... | iex as a supply chain risk: downloading and executing remote code without verification. The git clone approach lets you inspect claude-seo\install.ps1 before running it.

 Two versions. This public version is MIT licensed and free for everyone. AI Marketing Hub Pro members also get a private version with early access to new features. Members install it with:

 /plugin marketplace add AI-Marketing-Hub/claude-seo
/plugin install claude-seo@ai-marketing-hub-claude-seo
/seo setup

 Your first audit:

 claude # start Claude Code

/seo audit https://example.com # full site audit with a prioritized plan
/seo page https://example.com/pricing # one page, in depth
/seo geo https://example.com # how ready you are for AI search
/seo schema https://example.com # check and generate structured data
/seo local https://example.com # local SEO and Google Business Profile

 FAQ

 What is Claude SEO?

 A free, open-source SEO audit tool that runs inside Claude Code. It checks technical SEO, Core Web Vitals, content quality, Schema.org structured data, AI search readiness, local SEO, e-commerce and international SEO, then gives you a prioritized action plan. It follows Google's own documentation, including the AI Optimization Guide .

 Is it really free?

 Yes. It is MIT licensed, with no per-site pricing, no usage limits and no tracking. You only need Claude Code. A few optional extensions connect to paid services where you bring your own account, but everything works without them.

 Do I need API keys?

 No. Claude SEO works out of the box. If you want real field data, you can connect free Google APIs (PageSpeed Insights, Chrome UX Report, Search Console and Google Analytics 4) with /seo google setup . Your keys stay on your machine.

 How does it help with AI search like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT?

 Google says optimizing for AI search is still SEO, so Claude SEO starts with the basics that AI answers rely on: being indexed, fast and clear. Then /seo geo scores how easy your pages are to quote, checks that AI crawlers can reach them and looks at your brand's presence on Wikipedia, Reddit, YouTube and LinkedIn. /seo agentic checks how well AI agents can use your site.

 Does it work on JavaScript sites like Next.js, React or Vue?

 Yes. When a page needs JavaScript to show its content, Claude SEO opens it in a headless browser automatically, so single-page apps are audited as visitors see them.

 How is it different from Screaming Frog or other SEO tools?

 Crawlers like Screaming Frog crawl faster and deeper, and big SEO suites have their own backlink databases. Claude SEO does something else: it explains what it finds, sorts it by impact, covers AI search in depth and lets you ask follow-up questions in plain English. Many people use both.

 Does my data leave my computer?

 Claude SEO runs inside Claude Code, so the pages and data it analyzes are sent to Claude, Anthropic's model, the same as anything else you work on in Claude Code. Reports are saved as files on your machine. No SEO service or other third party sees your data unless you connect an extension or API yourself. Besides the site you audit, some checks read public sources such as Wikipedia, Reddit and Common Crawl. See PRIVACY.md for the full list.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
security-audit

 A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

 This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness . The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

 What it does

 The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

- Reconnaissance -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in architecture.md and coverage-ledger.json .

- Coverage-led hunting -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.

- Candidate validation -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.

- Structured output -- write confirmed , needs_validation , and rejected records to findings.json and validate them against report-schema.json .

- Independent record verification -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.

- Target-neutral reporting -- derive REPORT.md , FINDINGS-DETAIL.md , and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md from the verified records and coverage ledger.

 The parent runs validate-coverage-ledger.cjs after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs validate-findings.cjs in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

 The verdicts are distinct: confirmed has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, needs_validation has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and rejected records a disproved candidate.

 Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

 Files

 File
 Purpose

 SKILL.md
 Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns

 RECONNAISSANCE.md
 Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions

 HUNTING.md
 Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules

 ATTACK-CLASSES.md
 Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts

 MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md
 Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets

 AI-AND-LLM.md
 Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets

 WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md
 HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets

 CLIENT-SIDE.md
 DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets

 SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md
 Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes

 CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md
 IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes

 PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md
 RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes

 RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md
 Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes

 DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md
 Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes

 DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md
 Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes

 VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md
 Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting

 report-schema.json
 JSON schema for all three findings.json verdicts

 validate-findings.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for findings.json in Phases 4 and 5

 validate-findings.test.cjs
 Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks

 validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for coverage-ledger.json in Phases 1–5

 validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs
 Coverage-ledger validator tests

 Installation

 Install the skill with the Skills CLI :

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit

 Use --global for a user-level installation:

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit \
 --global

 Run npx skills --help for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

 Usage

 Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

 security audit this codebase

 find security vulnerabilities in ./src

 do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project

 The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N> . The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

 Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents

- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators

- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as needs_validation instead of executing target code.

 Design principles

- Only confirm established boundary failures. Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as needs_validation with its exact unresolved fact.

- Adversarial validation. The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.

- Severity requires impact. Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.

- Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities. If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.

- Multiple runs improve coverage. In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

 Contact

 Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

 MIT -- see LICENSE .
